title: F0 estimator octave-up failure on harmonic-rich frames
hypothesis: The YIN CMND estimator in src/vhe/data/f0.py picks the first dip below 0.15, so a harmonic-rich voiced frame whose dominant partial is an even multiple of f0 can be read one octave high (f0=220 Hz with a formant near 880 Hz reads 441 Hz). Hypothesis: choosing the smallest lag whose CMND is within 0.02 of the global minimum removes octave-up errors on harmonic-comb stimuli and on synthesized /a/ at 200-240 Hz, keeps pure-tone accuracy, does not introduce octave-down errors, and leaves the silence/noise gating results unchanged.

notes: Completed. Estimator-only probe; no torch, no real audio, no listening test. Adopted rule: bounded second-dip search with OCTAVE_TOLERANCE=0.02 and OCTAVE_DEPTH_RATIO=0.5. Residual defects documented in README (23% comb sub-multiple dips, 13% octave-up under 10 dB SNR, plus the E5 harmonic locking case).

errata: E1: probe_octave.py (v1) let the fundamental fall up to 29 dB below the dominant partial, so 799/1410 comb frames were scored 'other' while the estimator reported a real harmonic. v2 probe adds a -12 dB fundamental floor and reports CMND at the nominal and half period. v1 logs kept unchanged.

E2: the first implemented fix (restart from the global CMND minimum) was measured and reverted: 87 comb / 13 vowel / 40 robust octave-down frames versus 0 before. probe_after.json documents that discarded rule.
E3: the first implementation of the bounded rule compared array indices instead of lags and never fired; fixed before any number was recorded as a result.
Thresholds OCTAVE_TOLERANCE=0.02 and OCTAVE_DEPTH_RATIO=0.5 were selected on this stimulus set after seeing the sweep; the selection is not pre-registered and not validated on real speech.

E5: harmonic locking is a second, separate failure class found during P1.2 acceptance: with the default 65-900 Hz search range, /a/ reads 842 Hz at f0=210 Hz (F1 near 4*f0) and 902 Hz at f0=300 Hz (F1 near 3*f0); fmax_hz=500 recovers 210.5/300.7 Hz. Not fixed here; recorded as an appendix in the README and as a documented assertion in tests/test_synth_mandarin.py.
